title: Token Flow Stability Playbook — Diurnal & Microburst Capacity (Q4 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook to translate traffic projections into GPU allocation targets for the Hosted API across diurnal peaks and unpredictable microbursts. Focus: tokens/sec and QPS headroom targets, per-region readiness, and short-form runbook steps for on-call response and prewarm tactics.

Executive summary (short):
- Baseline steady-state: 1.25M tokens/sec global (current steady average across all models)
- Projected 95th percentile diurnal peak (Q4-2026 baseline traffic growth): 3.1M tokens/sec
- Microburst planning: design for 30% of regional peak to arrive in <15 min windows (worst-case scenario)
- Headroom policy: target 1.6x base peak capacity on dedicated pools OR 1.4x with aggressive prewarm + cross-region fallbacks enabled

Key assumptions (read first):
- Token to QPS conversion uses model-specific avg tokens per request (TPR). We use conservative TPRs by model class: tiny=32, small=128, medium=512, large=2048.
- Average request mix: 55% small/medium chat, 25% embeddings, 20% long generations (large).
- GPU performance throughput: A100-80GB baseline numbers measured in lab (conservative): tiny 120k tps, small 55k tps, medium 18k tps, large 3.8k tps (tps = tokens/sec per GPU). H100 performance scaled +30% over A100 for same precision and batching.
- KV-cache effectiveness: 10% token savings on chat-heavy routes if cacheable prefixes >20 tokens.
- Autoscaler cooldowns and prewarm windows: 2–6 min for warm slices, 8–15 min for full model weight transfer depending on region/cloud.

Quick conversion cheat-sheet:
- tokens/sec -> nominal GPUs needed per model class = ceil(tokens/sec / tps_per_gpu)
- QPS estimate = tokens/sec / (avg tokens per request)
- Example: 300k tokens/sec of medium-class traffic -> 300k / 18k = 16.7 -> 17 GPUs

Per-region projected windows (Q4-2026 scenario):
- us-west (primary traffic): baseline steady 540k tps, diurnal 95th 1.35M tps, microburst 15-min shock 1.75M tps
- us-east: baseline 320k tps, diurnal 95th 820k tps, microburst 15-min 1.05M tps
- eu-central: baseline 210k tps, diurnal 95th 540k tps, microburst 15-min 690k tps
- ap-southeast: baseline 180k tps, diurnal 95th 430k tps, microburst 15-min 560k tps

GPU fleet guidance (current mix & suggested tilt):
- Current fleet mix (approx): 60% A100-80GB, 30% H100, 10% L4/L40S for cheap embed-only workloads.
- Suggested short-term tilt: shift +10% capacity to H100 for burst-heavy queues and latency-critical small-medium models. H100 reduces headroom needed due to higher tps.
- Warm pool sizing: maintain 8–12% of regional steady-state as immediately warm (no weight transfer), an additional 12–18% in prewarm-only state (weights fetch but not fully warmed).

Headroom policy (novel metrics introduced):
- Stability Factor (σs): a composite multiplier capturing both diurnal variability and microburst probability. Calculate per-region: σs = 1 + diurnal_adder + microburst_hedge. Example us-west σs = 1 + 0.55 + 0.3 = 1.85 (diurnal adder = 55% above baseline; microburst hedge = 30%).
- Operational headroom = max(1.6, σs) for regions without cross-region fallback. If cross-region fallback is enabled and latency budget allows, usable headroom target can be lowered to max(1.35, σs * 0.85).

Microburst choreography (15-min windows):
- Prewarm triggers: latency heatmap exceeding threshold (P95 latency increase > 12%) OR ingress token rate spike > 20% in 60s.
- Short-circuit fallback: if prewarm cannot complete before target, route least-latency-sensitive traffic to best-effort pool (reduced cost QPS but higher latency) — use tagging at ingress layer.
- KV-cache aggressive mode: when microburst detected, switch to cache-first policy for chat routes to reduce duplicate prefix decoding (~10–20% tokens saved).

Cost vs reliability knobs (tradeoffs):
- Always-on headroom (no fallback): highest reliability, cost = baseline * stability factor.
- Hybrid headroom + cross-region fallback: 15–25% cost reduction vs always-on, adds complexity in routing and stateful sessions.
- Cache-first & batching increase effective throughput but can raise 99th latency if batching windows lengthen — apply only to non-interactive endpoints.

Runbook snippets (on-call):
- Detection: Alert INF-TPS-REGION-THRESHOLD when regional tps > diurnal_95th * 1.1 for 3 consecutive minutes.
- Immediate steps: 1) verify telemetry (ingress, prewarm, allocation logs), 2) enable cross-region fallback for the impacted route, 3) toggle KV-cache aggressive mode if chat-heavy, 4) escalate to capacity on-call to spin emergency warm slices.
- Escalation thresholds: if latency P95 > 2x SLO or error rate > 1% for 5 minutes, declare Capacity Incident and notify SRE + Product.

Sample capacity calculator (handy examples):
- us-west diurnal 95th = 1.35M tps. If 60% of that is medium-class (avg tpr=512), then medium tokens = 810k tps -> GPUs @ 18k tps = 45 GPUs.
- Add headroom policy (σs=1.85) -> provision 45 * 1.85 ≈ 84 GPUs regionally (round up to 86).
- If 30% H100 in pool (H100 tps = A100 * 1.3), effective GPU count can be reduced by ~10–12 GPUs depending on exact mix.

Open questions / items to validate quickly:
- Are our lab tps numbers for A100/H100 measured with the same batching/sequence length assumptions used in traffic forecasts? (owner: Arjun)
- Can prewarm weight transfer times be reduced below 6 min in eu-central by using local object storage mirrors? (owner: Leah)
- Slack UX: confirm that cross-region fallback is acceptable for customers in EU for short durations; product OK? (owner: Diego)

Action items (short list):
- [ ] Run microburst synthetic tests targeting 25% > diurnal-95th for 15 minutes in us-west (owner: Arjun, due: 2026-08-17)
- [ ] Generate per-route TPR estimates using production logs (owner: Maya, due: 2026-08-12)
- [ ] Draft customer-facing note for planned cross-region fallback capability (owner: Diego, due: 2026-08-20)

Notes to self / informal:
- This doc is intentionally lightweight — core deliverable is a small spreadsheet with per-region numbers + quick knobs. I will attach spreadsheet once per-route TPRs are computed.
- Keep microburst thresholds conservative until synthetic tests confirm cache-first savings.

Appendix (short):
- Reference metrics: SLOs we target: P95 latency < 350ms (small models), <750ms (medium), error rate <0.2%.
- Measurement tags to use: metric.namespace=ingress.tokens, metric.region, metric.model_class, metric.kv_cache_hit_ratio.

End of notes.
